Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system."] [:db/add "22f5a49d-093c-5c2d-bc11-d9f90e179350" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

$$

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-1 \\ y &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$
x-2(1)=-1\,⇒\,x=1.
$$

\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-13 \\ 2x+4y &=14.\end{aligned}\right.

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system."] [:db/add "41e257a6-c5ae-5b7a-8b67-a792cbbe038b" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 2 & 4 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 2 & 4 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 0 & 10 & 40\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-13 \\ y &=4,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=4$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(4)=-13\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=-2 \\ 4x-7y &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-1 \\ y &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(1)=-1\,⇒\,x=1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=1.$

\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-13 \\ 2x+4y &=14.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 2 & 4 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 2 & 4 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 0 & 10 & 40\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -13 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-13 \\ y &=4,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=4$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(4)=-13\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=4.$
